items.title: [FDD Diary #10] Running Everything by Hand
content:
Every day. Open the spec. Fix it. Throw it at the AI.
Check the result. Fix the spec.
Update PROBLEMS.md.
Refresh the project doc.
Throw it at the AI again.

This loop. Every day. Manually.

Forget one step and it breaks.
Don't log in PROBLEMS.md? Get hit in the same spot.
Don't update the project doc? AI builds from scratch.

"Do I have to do this every single time?"

Added a feature. AI built it in Python.
Next day, similar feature. AI built it in TypeScript.

"Yesterday was Python."
"Yes, Python was more suitable yesterday."

Same project.

Another one. "Build the agent system."
AI dumped a thousand lines. All at once.
Ran it. Blew up. No idea where.

Fix one thing, another breaks. Fix that, another breaks.

Two things were missing between spec and implementation.
Tech decisions. Task decomposition.
No Plan. No Tasks.

Tried it myself.

"This feature uses TypeScript. Runs on Rust runtime. Uses the existing transport module."
Wrote that down before throwing it at the AI.
Python stopped showing up.

Broke the big thing into small pieces.
Built one piece at a time.
One piece breaks? Fix that piece. The rest stayed intact.

Specify -> Plan -> Tasks -> Implement.
Four stages.

It had a name.
Spec-Driven Development. SDD.
"Write first. Build later."

items.title: [FDD Diary #11] Words Evaporate
content:
So I made a CLAUDE.md.

A file the AI reads automatically at the start of every session.
Wrote this in it:

"The spec for this project is here."
"The existing feature list is here."
"Make a Plan before writing code."
"Don't build everything at once. Break it into Tasks."

Now I don't have to say it every time.
The environment says it.

Words evaporate.
Environment stays.

No matter how good your prompts are.
One well-set-up work environment beats them all.

A spec went from document to system.

Not "I told the AI what to do."
"The environment tells the AI what to do."

That's the difference between a prompt and a system.

items.title: [FDD Diary #12] Repetition Worked. But...
content:
The SDD loop was running.

New feature: file change detection.
Specify. Plan. Tasks. Implement.
Four pieces. Built in order. Two days. Done.

Before? No spec. AI would've built from scratch.
Ignored existing modules. Collided with existing code.
A week.

After? Same feature built once. Because SSOT existed.
Three hours became forty-five minutes. Because PROBLEMS.md existed.
Error rate 40% became 5%. Because Plan locked the tech.

Wrote rules in CLAUDE.md.
"No coding without decisions."
"Spec first. Build later."
"Check existing code before starting."

The AI changed.
Stopped building from scratch.
Checks existing code first.
Asks about anything not in the spec.

Not a kindergarten teacher anymore.
A system was running.

Growth. Absolutely.

But the code started growing.

Five thousand lines became ten thousand.
Ten thousand became twenty thousand.

SDD covered "what to build."
But I opened the user settings screen.
Agent status was showing there.

Why is this here?
